question: How search engines rank pages

sources.title: In-depth guide to how Google Search works
notes: Discovery, crawling, indexing and serving are separate stages.
A crawled page is not guaranteed to be indexed or served.
Google selects canonical representatives from near duplicate pages.

sources.title: How Does Google Determine Ranking Results
notes: Intent, relevance, source quality, usability and context influence results.
Signal weights depend on the query: freshness matters more for news than stable definitions.
Advertising does not purchase organic position.

sources.title: A guide to Google Search ranking systems
notes: PageRank remains part of core ranking but has changed since its initial version.
Modern systems include BERT, RankBrain, passage-level understanding and deduplication.
Site-wide signals do not guarantee the ranking of an individual page.

sources.title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
notes: E-E-A-T is not one standalone ranking factor.
Human quality raters evaluate the systems but do not directly assign individual rankings.
Trustworthiness is particularly consequential for high-impact queries.

sources.title: The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine
sources.publisher: Sergey Brin and Lawrence Page, Stanford University
notes: Early Google combined full-text retrieval and hyperlink structure.
Historical PageRank should not be confused with a modern complete ranking formula.

uncertainties: Exact current ranking weights and proprietary implementation details are undisclosed.
Vendor explanations are primary statements of their systems, not independently audited reverse engineering.
